report:
What changed:      RESULTS.md (generated), benchmarks/make_results.py (new generator script)
What was measured: 3 of 5 rows (run1, run2, run3), n=3 each, from benchmarks/runs/run1.json, run2.json, run3.json (dated 2026-10-20 and 2026-10-21). Columns: tokens/s and TTFT ms. Limits: one model, one machine, decode speed and TTFT only.
What surprised me: run3 (20 GPU layers) is 3.1x slower than run1 (40.2 vs 125.7 tokens/s) and TTFT triples (388 vs 127 ms); the partial offload costs more than the q8 vs q4 step (110.4 vs 125.7).
Still [TODO]:      run4 (q8_0, 20 layers) and run5 (f16, all) have no run files; their tokens/s, TTFT and n are [TODO]. No commit hash or environment freeze is recorded in any run file, so the "freeze before you run" proof is [TODO]. Machine, GPU, prompt length and what n=3 averages over are not stated in the JSON.
The honest loss:   The table covers only 3 of 5 configurations; two rows are empty and the run files carry no commit or hardware fields, so none of the three numbers can be tied to a frozen environment.
